paper_title: VisuoThink Empowering LVLM Reasoning with Multimodal Tree Search
caption: (LEFT) The trend of Pass@1 rate on Visual Navigation as the number of reasoning steps increases. (right) The relationship between the Accuracy@1 on geometry problems (Geomverse) and tree width for rollout search. We observe that LVLMs significantly benefit from longer reasoning chains, although the effect plateaus rapidly beyond a certain threshold of reasoning steps. The relationship between performance and tree width exhibits a more complex pattern, demonstrating an inverted U-shaped trend with both GPT-4o and Claude-3.5-Sonnet.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the trend of Pass@1 rate on Visual Navigation as the number of reasoning steps increases. The y-axis represents the Pass@1 Rate as a percentage, with a linear scale ranging from 0 to 100%, and tick labels at intervals of 20%. The x-axis represents the Number of Reasoning Steps, with a linear scale ranging from 5 to 40, and tick labels at intervals of 5, 10, 20, and 40. The plot features two lines: one for GPT-4o, which is blue with circular markers and a solid line style, and one for Claude-3.5-Sonnet, which is light blue with cross-shaped markers and a solid line style. The GPT-4o line starts at 6.5% at 5 reasoning steps and increases to 32.3% at 10 steps, then to 77.4% at 20 steps, and finally to 83.9% at 40 steps. The Claude-3.5-Sonnet line starts at 19.4% at 5 reasoning steps and increases to 38.7% at 10 steps, then to 87.1% at 20 steps, and finally to 89.2% at 40 steps.
